facts: Four of the seven accused persons whose conviction u/s. 302 IPC and the sentence of life imprisonment has been affirmed by the High Court of Chhattisgarh have filed the instant appeals challenging Judgment and Order dated 30th November, 2009 of the High Court.

The short case of the prosecution is that on 05.12.2000 at about 8.55 p.m., Santosh (PW-4) lodged a FIR in the Ambikapur Police Station stating that a short while ago i.e. at about 8.40 p.m. while he was standing in front of his house along with deceased Vinod and Amit (PW-13), accused Gopi Ghasia(A-6) and Ranu(A-5) had come there in a state of intoxication.
According to the first informant, an altercation took place in the course of which he as well as Vinod had slapped accused Gopi. Enraged, the accused persons went away threatening to kill them.
The crime alleged was duly investigated and on completion thereof all the seven accused were charge sheeted under Section 147, 148, 302/149 of IPC.
As the accused claimed innocence a regular trial was held, at the conclusion of which all the seven accused were found guilty of the charge under Section 147, 148, 302/149 IPC.
issues: The liability of the accused appellants for the offence u/s. 302 IPC on the basis of their constructive liability, if any, u/s. 149 IPC
court_reasoning: The purport and effect of the provisions of S. 149 IPC has received the consideration of this court on more than one occasion.
An assembly of five or more persons having as its common object any of the five objects enumerated u/s. 141 of the IPC is deemed to be an unlawful assembly.
Membership of an unlawful assembly is itself an offence punishable u/s. 143 whereas other species of the said offence are dealt with u/ss. 143 to 145 of the IPC.
holding: The accused appellants, all or any of them, on the principle of vicarious or constructive liability u/s. 149 of the IPC.
